Its per-node worker, replicated.rs::run_backward_node_replicated, never names slot_increments at all. So on an enumerated traversal no binding increment is ever produced, allreduced, or recorded. Meanwhile DCS is fully wired on the enumerated FORWARD: forward/enumerated.rs:327-354 calls build_initial_resident_set then lazy_solve_preloaded, :288 and :546 gate fusion and basis capture on params.dcs, and :1018 passes training_ctx.dcs.filter(|p| p.is_active(iteration)) into the stage worker; setup/mod.rs contains zero occurrences of 'dcs', so the admission gate neither rejects nor mentions the enumerated-plus-DCS combination. The architectural defect is that contributing binding metadata is an undeclared per-driver duty -- hand-copied into two drivers and simply absent from the third -- rather than a step of the shared successor-outcome contract, so a driver omits it silently and no gate notices.

candidates.fixShape: Two roads, and the pick is the owner's because it turns on whether enumerated-plus-DCS is a supported combination. Road (a), make the exclusion explicit: reject the combination in the study admission gate exactly as the by-node scheduler's DCS exclusion is already handled, and pin it with a named test plus a rules entry, so an unsupported combination is a rejection rather than a silent degradation. Road (b), make the channel driver-independent: fold the slot_increments contribution into the shared outcome-aggregation step every backward driver already calls, so the replicated driver cannot omit it, and give the enumerated backward the per-stage allreduce that sync_stage_metadata performs on the sampled path. Road (a) is the smaller and the reversible one and matches the existing precedent; road (b) is the durable one if enumerated-plus-DCS is meant to work. Byte-neutrality bar: road (a) is byte-neutral by construction on every currently-passing configuration, since it only converts a silently-degraded run into a rejected one. Road (b) is NOT byte-neutral in solver statistics, because a differently-seeded DCS resident set changes the LP-solve count; it must remain byte-neutral in cuts, bounds and reported objective, which the parity goldens plus the rank-invariance harness and mpiexec -n 1 versus -n 2 verify, and which holds because the DCS lazy loop is exact. positives.subject: The storage, inflow-lag and transit-bucket state families in crates/cobre-sddp/src/lp/builder/columns.rs (fill_storage_columns, fill_ar_lag_columns, fill_transit_bucket_columns) versus the anticipated-commitment family
positives.why: The class sweep for the CD-074 shape finds no second instance, and the reason is structural rather than incidental. The shape requires a pinned incoming state coupled by a no-slack equality to a DIFFERENT column that carries a finite enforced bound, so that solver-scale drift on the pinned value can push the coupled column past a real cap and turn a feasible LP into a false infeasibility. Each of the three other families fails that test at the build site, which is the correct reason for having no reconciliation and no tolerance constants: incoming storage is left unconstrained at build time and pinned only by column bounds at solve time; the AR lag columns are unconstrained and signed, so no drift can cross a bound; and the reachable transit-bucket columns are bounded below by zero with no finite upper bound, with masked unreachable slots pinned to a degenerate zero range, so any drift at a bucket bound is an absolute-tiny quantity near zero and inside the backend's own primal feasibility tolerance rather than a relative quantity on a large megawatt cap. The anticipated-commitment family is the only one whose carried state is forced by an equality onto a generation column with a finite enforced upper bound, which is exactly why the reconciliation exists there and only there. Consequence for the question asked: a shared drift-handling seam would today have exactly one consumer, which is the one-consumer-abstraction trigger, so the answer is that drift handling should NOT be hoisted into a shared seam at this baseline. The defect CD-074 already records is the mechanism and its hard-coded constants within that single family, not the absence of a cross-family owner.

_needsHuman: Is enumerated traversal combined with dynamic cut selection a SUPPORTED configuration? The two roads in the first candidate diverge on this and only the owner can pick. If it is supported, the enumerated backward needs a binding-metadata contribution and its own per-stage allreduce, which changes DCS resident-set seeding and therefore the LP-solve count on existing enumerated-plus-DCS runs (cuts, bounds and objective stay byte-identical). If it is not supported, the combination should be rejected in the study admission gate and pinned with a named test, the way the by-node scheduler's DCS exclusion already is. Today it is neither: it runs, and it silently seeds the resident set by cut age alone.
